title: Digging
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Thursday's tide. Gully digs clams on the flats with a shovel and a bucket. Wood draws the holes, not the clams. Twenty holes. The strip counts them. The uncle, from the launch, counts the bucket.

panels.composition: The flats at the minus tide, Thursday. GULLY with a shovel, bent. A bucket. Holes behind him in a line. WOOD and BARNABY.

image.prompt: a stocky teenager digging on a mudflat with a shovel and a bucket, a line of holes behind him, a young man and a dog nearby, black and white, no words

panels.composition: A hole, close: the shovel's cut, water seeping in, a show of sand.

image.prompt: close on a freshly dug hole in wet mud with water seeping into it, black and white, no words

panels.composition: WOOD's pad: holes. A row. Numbered small at each one. Twenty.

image.prompt: close on a drawing pad with a row of small dug holes drawn and tiny numbers beside each, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The launch. The UNCLE on his pot with the bucket, counting into it. Gully, Wood, the dog coming in across the mud. Thursday's the one that matters, and the strip drew the holes.

image.prompt: an old man on a crab pot counting clams in a bucket as two figures and a dog cross a mudflat toward a boat launch, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Twenty holes, counted. The uncle counts the bucket.
